description: A GitHub Actions-compatible background worker that selects songs from dataset/Hooktheory.json.gz, synthesizes chord-and-melody audio, and renders piano-roll/falling-note videos with all piano keys visible. It tracks generated song IDs across runs and stores outputs in the repository.

services.name: Music video generator

questions.answer: Read the supplied compressed Hooktheory dataset; select songs deterministically; synthesize chord and melody audio; render a piano-roll/falling-notes video showing the full keyboard, with an FL Studio-inspired visual treatment; skip song IDs already in a persisted ledger; and save videos plus ledger updates in the repository. questions.question: Which stores should the MVP use for the duplicate ledger and generated videos?

options.label: SQLite
options.description: Persist the generated-song ID ledger as a local database that GitHub Actions can restore and commit.

options.label: Git-tracked repository files
options.description: Keep generated videos and any small state files in the repository; consider repository size and Git LFS limits.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Use object storage for media if repository growth, artifact limits, or download needs make Git storage impractical.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: No persistent ledger or artifact storage.

questions.rationale: The user explicitly requests persistent duplicate tracking and repository-stored videos. SQLite and tracked files meet that intent; Blob Storage is included as a scale-out option because generated videos are media and GitHub/repository size limits need a practical fallback.
